html:
In 1488 the Portuguese captain Bartolomeu Dias sailed round the southern tip of Africa, proving there was a sea route from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean.

Portugal had been working down the African coast for decades; Diogo Cão had reached the Congo river a few years before. Dias left Lisbon in 1487 for King João II. Storms carried him south out of sight of land, and when he turned east he found the coast running east, then north. He landed at Mossel Bay early in 1488. His crew forced him to turn back soon after, and on the way home he sighted the Cape of Good Hope.

Ten years later Vasco da Gama followed the route all the way to India. The arrival at Calicut opened direct European trade in the Indian Ocean. Dias himself died in a storm near the Cape in 1500.
sum: In 1488 the Portuguese captain Bartolomeu Dias sailed round the southern tip of Africa, proving there was a sea route from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean.
